Last month, OpenAI previewed hardware products under its Codex brand. Today, the company officially announced the result of its collaboration with Work Louder — the Codex Micro keyboard, priced at US$230.

The product is introduced as follows:

The keyboard comes in two versions: a tactile version and a silent version.

The website states: "Each Agent key displays different RGB lighting effects based on Codex's real-time status, so you can see at a glance which Agent is thinking, running, waiting, or has finished its work, and then switch conversations."

The product page also lists three Codex-exclusive features:

  • Instant skill triggering: flick the joystick to launch commonly used Codex workflows, such as reviewing PRs, debugging, or refactoring code.
  • Keep core actions at your fingertips: command keys provide dedicated shortcuts for your most frequently used operations, including accept, reject, conversation keys, new conversation, and more. Less switching, more efficiency.
  • Just say the word: twist the dial to instantly adjust reasoning intensity. Keep it high for simple tasks, crank it up when deeper thinking is needed.

Available for order from today, here. Plus a promo video:

That's roughly the gist. For both OpenAI and the hardware world, this month has been quite eventful.
